Moody’s: Bank Respublika-AccessBank merger to create Azerbaijan’s fourth-largest bank
sum: BAKU, Azerbaijan, November 14. Bank Respublika-AccessBank merger will create Azerbaijan’s fourth-largest bank, says Moody's.

On November 3, Bank Respublika and AccessBank announced the successful completion of a strategic transaction under which Bank Respublika acquired 100% of AccessBank’s shares, while AccessBank’s former shareholders became shareholders of Bank Respublika by receiving newly issued preference shares in Bank Respublika.

"Following completion of the acquisition, Bank Respublika and AccessBank will initially continue to operate as separate banks, with their subsequent integration into a single bank subject to applicable regulatory requirements. The merged entity will have a market share of around 7-8% of banking system assets in Azerbaijan, making it the country's fourth-largest bank by assets," said the rating agency.

Moody's analysts expect Bank Respublika's asset quality to come under pressure in 2026-2027, driven by the consolidation of AccessBank's loan book, which had a problem loan ratio of 7.4% at year-end 2025, and by differences in the two banks' underwriting standards.

"Before the merger Bank Respublika reported problem loan ratio of 1.4% at mid-2026 and problem loan coverage of 109%. Notwithstanding these immediate integration risks, we see potential for Bank Respublika to realize cost savings and synergies over the longer term. Both banks have similar business models and overlapping customer bases, with a focus on micro, SMEs and individuals. The combination of Bank Respublika's and AccessBank's franchises in Azerbaijan will give Bank Respublika greater scale and stronger bargaining power as the largest player in the micro and SME segments," reads the latest report by Moody's.
The rating agency expects the combined bank's funding profile to be more reliant on customer deposits than Bank Respublika's current funding profile.

"We also expect the combined bank to maintain adequate liquidity buffers over the next 12-18 months, supported by slower loan growth. The negative outlook on Bank Respublika's long-term deposit ratings indicates that an upgrade is unlikely over the next 12-18 months.

LEG Immobilien stock: 2027 AFFO outlook points to further growth
sum: Компания LEG Immobilien подтвердила свои финансовые цели на 2026 год в четверг, 12 ноября, и представила свой первый прогноз на 2027 год. В своем отчете по связям с инвесторами LEG, опубликованном в тот же день, говорится, что скорректированные средства от операционной деятельности достигли 190,1 миллиона евро за первые девять месяцев 2026 года, что на 4,9 процента больше, чем за период предыдущего года.

LEG ожидает, что за весь 2026 год AFFO составит от 220 до 240 миллионов евро. Руководство прогнозирует, что на 2027 год AFFO составит от 230 до 250 миллионов евро, при этом средняя точка предполагает дальнейшее увеличение на 4 процента. Компания заявила, что рост должен компенсировать компенсирующие эффекты, включая более высокие процентные расходы.

Сопоставимый рост арендной платы достиг 3,9 процента за первые девять месяцев, в то время как уровень вакантных площадей EPRA упал до 2,5 процента. В 2027 году LEG ожидает, что рост арендной платы снизится до 2,9–3,1 процента, и планирует инвестиции в размере около 35 евро за квадратный метр.

LEG также сообщила, что все сроки погашения финансирования рассчитаны до осени 2027 года. В сентябре агентство Moody's повысило рейтинг компании до Baa1 со стабильным прогнозом. Компания больше не ожидает достижения LTV около 45 процентов в 2026 году, ссылаясь на давление со стороны оценки недвижимости и снижение объемов транзакций.

Акции LEG Immobilien торговались по цене 49,25 евро на бирже Lang & Schwarz в 18:06 по центральноевропейскому времени в пятницу, 13 ноября 2026 г., что на 0,26 процента выше цены закрытия Xetra в четверг, 13 ноября 2026 г.

Инвесторы сопоставляют новые перспективы роста денежных потоков с ожидаемым замедлением роста арендной платы и отсрочкой цели по сокращению доли заемных средств. Объединение оставляет операционную динамику неизменной, сохраняя при этом финансирование и оценку недвижимости в центре инвестиционного проекта.
Немецкие акции остаются для LEG более широким рынком; см. текущие рыночные отчеты.

Moody’s downgrades Macau concessionaire SJM on “very high leverage” and near-term refinancing needs
sum: Moody’s Ratings has downgraded Hong Kong-listed Macau casino operator SJM Holdings Limited’s corporate family rating from B1 to B2, and the senior unsecured ratings on bonds issued by Champion Path Holdings Limited and SJM International Limited from B2 to B3, citing the group’s “very high leverage.”

In a note, Moody’s Ratings Senior Vice President Stephanie Lau said the downgrade “reflects SJM’s very high leverage, mainly driven by weak earnings amid a moderating gross gaming revenue (GGR) growth environment in Macau.
“The negative outlook reflects the uncertainty regarding the pace of deleveraging and the company’s significant refinancing needs over the next one to two years, which could weaken liquidity.”
Moody’s added that SJM’s leverage will remain elevated through 2027 because of the weaker industry GGR environment, the gradual pace of operating cost reductions, and its moderate market share.

Given the company’s moderate earnings, the ratings agency expects adjusted debt/EBITDA to increase from 9.0x in 2025 to 9.9x in 2026, before improving to around 9.0x in 2027 and 8.3x in 2028. However, the pace of deleveraging remains uncertain and will depend on the extent of the company’s earnings recovery and debt reduction.

“While we expect the company’s cost control efforts and the completion of existing renovations to support an earnings recovery over the next one to two years, the weaker industry GGR environment limits visibility into the pace and extent of the recovery,” Moody’s said.

“We expect Macau’s industry GGR to register a slight decline in 2026 and remain broadly flat in 2027. Against this backdrop, there is limited visibility into whether SJM’s leverage will improve toward or below 8.5x, the required threshold for the B2 corporate family rating.”

items.t: Moody’s Stock Nears a Breakout as Its Proprietary Data Gains Value in the AI Era
sum: Moody’s shares are approaching the upper end of a trading range that followed a sharp sell-off earlier this year, as investors reassess whether artificial intelligence poses a threat to the company’s credit ratings and data businesses—or could increase demand for them.

The stock fell more than 19% by mid-February and reached a low near $402. It has since recovered to $514.53, up about 10% over the past month and roughly 6% below its 52-week high of $547. Despite the rebound, Moody’s has been largely range-bound this year and is up less than 1% since January.

The sell-off came as investors worried that new AI tools could disrupt software and information-services companies. An Anthropic legal plug-in helped trigger a broad retreat across the sector, with ratings agencies, data providers and index companies among those that fell at least 5% intraday. Moody’s was caught up in the same concerns.

The company’s business is divided between Moody’s Investors Service, its credit-rating agency, and Moody’s Analytics, which sells data and risk-management products. In the third quarter, Investors Service generated $1.09 billion in revenue, supported by about $1.7 trillion of rated debt issuance. Analytics brought in $936 million from products that include credit-risk assessments, insurance catastrophe models and know-your-customer compliance data. The company said 99% of its revenue is recurring and reported $3.7 billion in annual recurring revenue.

Supporters of Moody’s argue that its proprietary information could become more valuable as businesses adopt AI. Many of the company’s datasets are not readily available from public sources, and AI systems rely on reliable information to produce useful outputs.

Chief Executive Rob Fauber said on the company’s third-quarter earnings call that customers are integrating Moody’s research into their own AI platforms. The number of users of its Model Context Protocol tools, which allow AI systems to access approved data sources, more than quadrupled in three months, while usage increased more than tenfold. Analysts using the tools were accessing three times as much content per day, Fauber said.

Nokia Shares Extend Three-Day Rally to Reclaim $8, Poised to Gain Over 10% in Near Term
sum: Nokia shares rose 0.86% to $8.25 on November 10 Eastern Time, extending a three-day rebound driven by tech sector recovery, oversold technical conditions, and AI optimism. Q3 AI and cloud revenue surged 123% year-over-year with €1.5 billion in order intake, while Moody’s upgraded Nokia’s credit rating to investment-grade Baa3. Technically, the stock is testing key resistance near $8.40; breaking this level could target $9.39, whereas dropping below $7.90 support risks retesting the $7.36 low.

TradingKey - On November 10 Eastern Time, shares of Nokia (NOK) rose 0.86% to close at $8.25, after touching an intraday high of $8.39, with trading volume of approximately 57.26 million shares. Previously, on November 5, NOK plunged 9.69% in a single day to hit a low of $7.36, followed by a three-day rebound that gained roughly 12% from its recent low. In the latest overnight trading, the stock rose further to near $8.50, improving its short-term technical posture, though it has yet to fully break out of its medium-term corrective structure.

The recent sustained rebound in Nokia's share price has been driven primarily by a broader recovery in tech stocks, a technical bounce following prior oversold conditions, and expectations of growth in its AI business. On November 9, NOK's U.S. ADR gained 6.79% to $8.18, marking its second straight session of gains and outperforming the broader market over the same period.

From a fundamental perspective, the company's third-quarter revenue from AI and cloud customers surged 123% year-over-year, with related order intake reaching €1.5 billion, up 118% year-over-year, indicating that AI data center construction is generating fresh demand for its optical communications and IP networks businesses. In addition, Moody's recently upgraded Nokia's long-term credit rating from Ba1 to an investment-grade Baa3 while maintaining a positive outlook, which has also provided support for market confidence.

Looking at Nokia's daily stock chart, shares have rebounded for three consecutive trading sessions following November 5 and have now reclaimed the 5-day moving average. Meanwhile, the stock climbed above $8.50 in after-hours trading during the previous session.

Is Moody's (MCO) Already Overvalued After A 52% Three Year Gain?
sum: Moody's has seen its stock advance over the past few years, and investors now have to ask whether that price makes sense given the returns the business earns on the capital it deploys. A rich share chart on its own does not explain if those returns are strong enough to support paying more for each dollar invested in the company.
Over the past 3 years the stock has returned 52.4%, which puts real weight on the question of whether Moody's underlying return on capital fully supports that kind of share price gain.

The company relies heavily on turning its credit ratings and analytics franchises into high margin cash generation, so the durability of those margins is central to how efficiently each incremental dollar of capital can be put to work.
The issue now is whether the returns Moody's earns on its capital are strong and durable enough to justify where the stock trades today.
If you want to stress test this same question about the returns companies earn on their capital across a wider field, take a look at 33 high quality undervalued stocks.

The Excess Returns model looks at how profitably Moody's can reinvest shareholders' equity above its own funding cost. On this view, the company is projected to earn stable EPS of $19.70 per share against a cost of equity of $1.89 per share and book value of $18.95 per share. That implies an excess return of $17.81 per share and an average return on equity of 83.38%, which is very high compared with the equity base those earnings are being generated from.

Analysts feeding into the model also expect stable book value to rise to $23.63 per share over time, which keeps compounding those excess returns on a thicker equity layer. Even with that strong profitability profile, the Excess Returns projections put Moody's estimated intrinsic value meaningfully below the current share price of $511.08. As a result, anyone looking at the stock today is paying a full price for those projected economics. Find out what Moody's could be worth using our Excess Returns estimate.

European shares jump as Tech rebounds; Nvidia probe weighs
sum: Investing.com - European equities surged on Monday, with the benchmark STOXX 600 jumping 1% as investors seized on discounted semiconductor stocks and cheered a wave of Italian banking consolidation, shaking off early caution ahead of a data-heavy week.
The pan-European index reversed a dour morning start, driven by aggressive dip-buying across the technology sector.

Regional bourses tracked the broad advance, with Germany's DAX jumping 1.5%, France's CAC 40 adding 1.1%, and London's FTSE 100 rising 0.8%. Spain's bank-heavy IBEX 35 also rode the financial sector's powerful tailwind to rise 1.9%.

Monday's rally was heavily concentrated in Europe's semiconductor and enterprise software franchises, which staged a fierce relief rally after being severely beaten down last week during a global liquidation in artificial intelligence assets.

Shares of ASML, ASM International, and Soitec gained over 2% each, while enterprise software leader SAP rose 1.8%. German chipmaker Infineon anchored the sector's outperformance, surging nearly 4% as buyers determined last week's post-election tech rout had pushed valuations into oversold territory.
The broad European tech advance notably ignored weakness emanating from the vanguard of the AI boom.

Frankfurt-listed shares of Nvidia tumbled 6% as markets digested reports that the chipmaker's board of directors has launched an independent investigation into founder and Chief Executive Jensen Huang.

Moody's Grants Nokia Investment-Grade Status as Hotwire Taps Vendor for AI-Ready Network
sum: Nokia shares advanced 3.5% on Friday, riding a broader rebound in technology and AI-related equities. Reports from AP described AI stocks clawing back part of their losses, while Reuters noted gains among chipmakers following a technology-driven selloff earlier in the week. Media coverage also pointed to an improved credit assessment as a factor shoring up sentiment around the Finnish network equipment maker, though no single trigger for the day's move could be pinpointed.

Moody's Ratings on Tuesday raised Nokia's long-term issuer rating and its assessment of senior unsecured obligations from Ba1 to Baa3. The agency kept its positive outlook in place, citing accelerating demand for cloud and AI infrastructure as the rationale. The decision covers both Nokia as an issuer and its senior unsecured debt, while the outlook was left untouched.
The upgrade lands alongside Nokia's third-quarter and nine-month interim report for 2026, published on October 22, in which the company reaffirmed its full-year financial guidance.

Separately, Nokia disclosed on Wednesday that Hotwire Communications had selected it to construct a next-generation network in North Carolina. The planned infrastructure is to be engineered for the demands of an AI networking architecture, with Hotwire expecting service to go live in early 2027. Nokia did not attach a contract value to the announcement.

Also on Wednesday, Nokia released its global network traffic report, projecting that artificial intelligence will account for 44% of worldwide traffic carried over networks by 2035. Total network traffic at that point is expected to reach nearly 3,789 exabytes per month. Those figures represent a long-range company forecast rather than traffic volumes already achieved, and the report underscores the growing infrastructure requirements driven by AI. No direct link between its publication and Friday's share price gain has been established; for the North Carolina project, early 2027 remains the next dated milestone cited.

A stake notification dated September 30 shows FMR LLC and Abigail P. Johnson holding economic interest in 3.8% of Nokia shares. The regulatory filing documents the ownership position but does not confirm any purchase of stock.

Nokia Shares Gain 3.5% as AI Networking Momentum Meets a Moody's Upgrade
sum: Nokia's stock closed Friday at €7.00, up 3.5%, as optimism around AI-driven telecom equipment and rising network traffic lifted sentiment. Media reports point to that broader enthusiasm as a possible backdrop for the move, though no single fresh catalyst has been confirmed as the trigger.

The advance followed a rebound in AI-related equities, which came on the heels of a two-day selloff, according to media accounts. Worries about spending levels in the AI sector and the prospect of regulation have not dissipated.

Roughly two weeks ago, Nokia reported third-quarter 2026 comparable net sales of €5,154 million, a 10% increase year over year by the company's own accounting. Comparable operating profit climbed 35% to €605 million. Management left its full-year outlook for comparable operating profit untouched, still projecting between €2.1 billion and €2.6 billion.

Among the week's concrete announcements, Hotwire Communications selected Nokia to construct a next-generation network in North Carolina. The build is designed to be ready for AI-based network architectures and will use Nokia's 7750 Service Router line. Activation is expected in early 2027. The order has not been established as the cause of the recent share-price gain.

Credit quality also moved in Nokia's favor this week. Moody's Ratings raised the company's long-term issuer rating and the rating on its senior unsecured obligations from Ba1 to Baa3, with the outlook remaining positive, according to media reports. The agency cited demand for cloud and AI infrastructure as well as Nokia's expanding network infrastructure business as the rationale.

Separately, Nokia published a long-range outlook on global network traffic. It projects that AI will account for 44% of worldwide network traffic by 2035, with total monthly data volume approaching 3,789 exabytes. The figures represent a corporate forecast rather than traffic volumes already recorded. While the Hotwire contract covers a specific build-out, the traffic report sets out Nokia's view of longer-term demand; early 2027 remains the next milestone on the North Carolina timeline.
Nokia and ICEYE also signed a letter of intent with Ukraine's defense ministry about two weeks ago. The parties will examine potential cooperation on sovereign satellite communications.

Danaos stock: Moody's lifts outlook to positive, notes to Ba1
sum: Danaos Corporation said on October 26, 2026, that Moody's Ratings had changed the outlook on its Ba1 Corporate Family Rating to positive from stable and upgraded its senior unsecured notes to Ba1 from Ba2. The company described the action in a Danaos Corporation investor release.

Moody's attributed the outlook change to higher revenue visibility, substantial cash balances and continued financial discipline. The rating agency also cited Danaos' long-term, fixed-rate charter portfolio, positive free cash flow track record and focus on reducing debt ahead of shareholder distributions.

As of June 30, 2026, Danaos had contracted revenue of approximately 4.6 billion US dollars, with an average remaining charter duration of 4.7 years. Cash stood at approximately 1.0 billion US dollars at that date, according to the company release.

Danaos' contracted charter base provides a degree of revenue visibility even if charter-market conditions weaken. That does not remove exposure to shipping cycles, but fixed-rate contracts can moderate the effect of short-term market swings on operating cash flow.
The real-time quote of Danaos stock was 135.60 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 23:00 CET on Wednesday, November 4, 2026.

Danaos is one of the largest independent owners of modern containerships and charters vessels to major liner companies on long-term agreements. Its fleet included 78 containerships with aggregate capacity of 502,265 TEUs, alongside 28 containerships under construction with capacity of 177,776 TEUs, according to the company release.

The company also has dry bulk exposure through 11 Capesize vessels and four Newcastlemax newbuildings. Danaos is headquartered in Cyprus and its shares trade on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker DAC.

items.t: Oracle stock slides as it borrows another $10 billion for AI spending
sum: Five days after Oracle (ORCL) promised to rein in its fundraising, it raised the full $20 billion in a single day.

Oracle kicked off a $10 billion bond sale Monday and, at the same time, filed to sell $10 billion of stock. Together, that's every dollar of new debt and stock it said at last week's investor day it would raise through fiscal 2030.

Investors didn't love the speed. Oracle stock fell nearly 9% Monday, its worst day since June, to its lowest close since July 29. That wiped out what was left of last week's 11% investor-day pop. Over three sessions, Oracle is down nearly 18%, its worst three-day stretch since 2002, by Yahoo Finance's calculations.

It's been a rough year. Oracle has lost more than half its value over the past 12 months, while Microsoft (MSFT), Amazon (AMZN), Alphabet (GOOGL), and Meta (META) are all within about 5% of where they started.
So is Oracle Big Tech's canary in the coal mine? Not really.

The company's big drops haven't been an early warning for the rest of the group. After Oracle's nine previous three-day plunges of 12% or more since 2016, Microsoft, Amazon, Alphabet, and Meta fell over the following month only four times, by Yahoo Finance's calculations. And at the tops of the dot-com bubble in 2000 and the pandemic boom in 2021, Oracle peaked after the Nasdaq, not before.
What sets Oracle apart is how it pays for the AI build-out. Follow the debt.

Editorial: It’s time for us to take stock of two elections
sum: As voters, we don’t always know who the candidates are or who will deliver on their promises. Often, it’s hard to connect with the contenders directly — the people who, if elected, will oversee policy and control the public purse.
In B.C., we’ve just come off back-to-back votes, so there’s been a lot of political messaging to wade through both municipally and provincially.
Let’s take a minute to catch our collective breath and review what we’ve just gone through.

On the civic front, we’ve got three new mayors in the seven communities we serve. And the provincial race ushered in a blue tsunami, with the Conservative Party of BC clinching three of the four seats in the Tri-Cities and two of the five in Burnaby.

In her last meeting as a city councillor, Trish Mandewo, who ran for the Coquitlam mayor’s chair, wept as she described the attacks against her during the seven-week race. She spoke about how her 22-year-old daughter had to hide the social media hatred so her mom could focus on running for public office.
MLAs also complained to Freshet News about the rage farming during the provincial campaign — digital posts designed to stir anger, outrage and fear.
We were told we would be a more caring, empathetic society in a post-pandemic world.

JPMorgan cuts Moody's target to USD 555 for Moody's stock
sum: JPMorgan Chase & Co. reduced its price target for Moody's from USD 570.00 to USD 555.00 on October 14, 2026, while retaining an Overweight rating, according to MarketBeat. The revision arrives one week before Moody's next quarterly report.

The lower target contrasts with Moody's latest reported operating picture. In the second quarter of 2026, revenue reached USD 2.19 billion, an increase of 15.10 percent from the same period a year earlier, while diluted earnings per share came to USD 5.03, according to MarketBeat. The company also set fiscal 2026 earnings-per-share guidance at USD 16.50 to USD 17.00.

For investors, the key test is whether the coming report supports that earnings path. MarketBeat cited a consensus target of USD 555.74 and a Moderate Buy rating, but those figures combine different analyst views and do not remove the questions reflected in the latest target reductions.

On July 22, 2026, Moody's reported second-quarter revenue of USD 2.19 billion and diluted earnings per share of USD 5.03, according to MarketBeat. On October 7, 2026, Morgan Stanley cut its target from USD 512.00 to USD 470.00. On October 14, 2026, JPMorgan Chase lowered its target from USD 570.00 to USD 555.00, with both analyst actions reported by MarketBeat.

Moody's will release third-quarter 2026 results before the NYSE opens on October 21, 2026, followed by an earnings conference call at 9:00 a.m. ET. The date and call details were announced by Moody's Corporation on September 30, 2026.

The scheduled report gives the market a near-term checkpoint for fiscal 2026 earnings guidance of USD 16.50 to USD 17.00. At Lang & Schwarz, Moody's stock was trading at EUR 415.50 on October 15, 2026 at 11:11 a.m. CEST.

sum: For much of this year, investors have been wrestling with a simple question: is a company this tied to debt market activity really worth owning at 26 times forward earnings when corporate borrowing could slow at any moment?
That skepticism has kept Moody’s Corporation (MCO) stock down roughly 5.5% year-to-date even as the broader market has moved higher.

The Q2 results, reported July 22, made that caution look misplaced. Moody’s posted $2.185 billion in revenue, up 15% year-over-year, driven by a significant tailwind from surging debt issuance across virtually every category.

As the revenue chart below shows, quarterly revenue has been climbing steadily, and while consensus expects some seasonal softness in the back half of 2026, the trajectory heading into 2027 remains positive.
CEO Rob Fauber noted that customers are turning to Moody’s “to make consequential decisions with greater confidence” as capital markets grow more complex.

Leveraged loan issuance volume jumped 53%, investment-grade volume rose 17%, and the Public, Project and Infrastructure Finance segment saw rated issuance volume grow 44%, driven by data center and technology infrastructure financing.
The market had been pricing in a cyclical slowdown. Instead, Moody’s delivered the opposite.

MIS adjusted operating margin reached 68.3%, up 410 basis points, as the business absorbed record volume without adding cost at the same pace. CEO Rob Fauber framed the scale of the beat directly on the Q2 2026 earnings call: “We achieved 15% revenue growth. We grew adjusted operating income by 25%, expanded adjusted operating margin by 440 basis points to 55.3% and we grew adjusted diluted EPS by 31% to $4.68, and that’s a great progression from the top line to the bottom line.”

Moody’s (MCO) Is One of Warren Buffett’s Longest-Held Holdings; See Why
sum: Moody's Corporation (NYSE:MCO) is among the best Warren Buffett stocks.
A closeup of hands signing a contract for a successful real estate loan.

Buffett added Moody's Corporation (NYSE:MCO) to his portfolio back in 2000, when the financial services company spun off from Dun & Bradstreet. As of Q4 2010, Warren Buffett held 28.42 million shares worth $754.14 million. Although reduced, the company's stake in Moody's remains significant. As of Q4 2025, Berkshire holds 24.67 million shares, which translates into a $12.60 billion stake.

Moody's Corporation (NYSE:MCO) is widely held by hedge funds as well, with 91 out of 1,041 hedge funds remaining bullish on the stock. The combined hedge fund stake in the stock totals $25.54 billion as of Q4 2025.

The bullish case for Moody's Corporation (NYSE:MCO) rests on regulatory privilege, embedded demand, and capital-light growth. As of April 20, 2026, over 80% of covering analysts keep bullish ratings on the stock, with the $535 consensus price target implying over 17% upside potential.

In its Q4 2025 investor letter, Ironvine Capital Partners, an independently owned, public equity management firm, argued that Moody's and S&P function almost as near monopolies within global debt markets, as U.S. and European authorities depend on their ratings when buying bonds and measuring risk. As a result, issuers that choose not to obtain these ratings often face higher borrowing costs.

This dynamic puts Moody's Corporation (NYSE:MCO) in a strong position to benefit from GDP-linked debt growth, which requires minimal capital. This leaves the company with room for share buybacks and dividend payments.

sum: Warren Buffett once wrote, "When we own portions of outstanding businesses with outstanding managements, our favorite holding period is forever." While Buffett constantly aimed to buy only wonderful businesses, few met the criteria for becoming the stocks Berkshire Hathaway (BRKA -0.36%) (BRKB +0.76%) would hold forever.

In his first letter to shareholders, Buffett's successor at Berkshire, Greg Abel, called out nine companies he describes as core holdings in the company's equity portfolio. Combined, they account for over 60% of the company's portfolio. Investors should expect "limited activity in these holdings," Abel said. Many of the stocks Abel mentioned align with previous comments from Buffett, but not all of them. Here are the nine stocks Abel plans to hold forever.

Apple (AAPL +2.43%) is Berkshire Hathaway's largest marketable equity position. That's despite Warren Buffett's decision to sell more than three-quarters of its shares over the last two years of his tenure as CEO. Apple's lower capital intensity compared to its big-tech peers has made it stand out so far in 2026. While hyperscalers are spending over $700 billion in combined capital expenditures to build out artificial intelligence (AI) data centers this year, Apple is on track for another year of free cash flow exceeding $100 billion.

Despite delays in its revamped Siri, meant to introduce more powerful AI features to its devices, Apple saw strong sales growth last quarter across both devices and services. iPhone sales, in particular, stood out, up 23% year over year, bolstered by strength in Greater China. If the Siri revamp is a success, it could post another strong year of iPhone sales this year as it spurs a major upgrade cycle.
While the stock may seem expensive at 30 times forward earnings, its share repurchase program, solid revenue growth, and expanding margins make it a fair price for the stock.

Moody’s flags $662 billion risk at the heart of the data center build-out by just 5 companies
sum: The technology sector's frantic race to build artificial intelligence infrastructure has created a massive, financial overhang. According to a recent in-depth report by Moody's Ratings, the top five U.S. hyperscalers have accumulated $662 billion in future data center lease commitments not yet begun that are not current liabilities and therefore sit entirely off their balance sheets. As those leases begin over the next several years, and as landlords' obligations are fulfilled, that more than half a trillion dollars' worth of data center activity will be recorded on balance sheets.

The report, which analyzed the financial disclosures of Amazon, Meta, Alphabet, Microsoft, and Oracle, highlights how the unprecedented build-out of AI data centers is straining traditional accounting metrics. As of the end of 2025, these five tech giants had amassed a staggering $969 billion in total undiscounted future lease commitments, or data centers that have yet to be built. However, more than two-thirds of this total, that $662 billion figure, is for leases that have yet to commence, meaning that under generally accepted accounting principles, or GAAP, these companies are not required to recognize these massive obligations on their current balance sheets.

To put the scale of this hidden obligation into perspective, Moody's accounting analysts David Gonzales and Alastair Drake calculated that the unrecorded $662 billion is equivalent to 113% of these five hyperscalers' most recent adjusted debt.

Gonzales told Fortune in a statement that it's "not as if [these hyperscalers] have have avoided a liability through structuring," characterizing the $662 billion at issue as "yet to be on the balance sheet," rather than missing. "More accurately," he added, "they have not yet received the services to trigger this liability as of this time, but they will."

For instance, Alphabet disclosed in a footnote in the third quarter of 2025 that it had "entered into leases primarily related to data centers that have not yet commenced with future lease payments of $42.6 billion, including a purchase option considered reasonably certain to be exercised, that are not yet recorded on our Consolidated Balance Sheet.

items.t: Markets and the economy are ‘increasingly disconnected,’ top economist warns
sum: An adage in investing and policymaking circles is the reminder that the markets are not the economy. While the former tracks profits and expectations, the latter busies itself with tangible stuff, from jobs and wages to GDP. Often the two can tell a similar story, but there are also times when they become disjointed, and economic fortunes get tied up with the whims of financial markets.
According to Mark Zandi, Moody’s Analytics’ prominent chief economist, we are now in one of those moments.

“I rarely weigh in on financial markets, as they generally reflect and are broadly consistent with economic conditions. But there are times when I feel markets are overdone and increasingly disconnected from the economy,” Mark Zandi wrote in an X thread Sunday.

The disconnect Zandi is talking about has left many analysts scratching their heads over the past year. While financial markets have performed well, including not only stocks but also commodities such as gold and silver, the economy as a whole seems to be in a bit of a lull, and has flashed more than a few warning signs. As the disconnect grows, propelled by high valuations and rising speculation in financial markets, Zandi cautioned that the real economy could be suffocated.

Real GDP growth in the U.S. decelerated sharply to just 1.4% in the last quarter of 2025, down from 4.4% in the previous quarter, the Commerce Department announced last week. This pace falls below the economy’s potential of around 2.5%, Zandi wrote, signaling unsustainable momentum. Job market indicators further underscore the rift. Unemployment ticked down slightly to 4.3% last month from 4.4% in December, and employers added more jobs than expected in January, but revised 2025 estimates released this month suggested almost no job growth at all last year.

Those factors do not paint a particularly rosy economic picture. But in the background, financial markets keep punching above their weight. Fueled by strong returns last year, expected rate cuts and artificial intelligence hype, many analysts project 2026 to be another banner year for assets. Researchers from Goldman Sachs, for instance, expect the S&P 500 to rise 12% this year.

items.t: Top Wide-Moat Stocks to Invest in for Long-term Growth
sum: A wide moat refers to companies with lasting competitive advantages that protect them from rivals, similar to how a moat defends a castle. Made famous by Warren Buffett, this strategy targets businesses that can sustain strong long-term profitability due to factors like distinct market positions, strong brand loyalty, cost advantages, network effects and regulatory barriers.

Among the companies that exemplify wide economic moats are Lam Research Corporation LRCX, NVIDIA Corporation NVDA, ASML Holding N.V. ASML and Moody's Corporation MCO. These companies compete in industries with significant barriers to entry, which safeguard their market positions and promote consistent revenue growth by reducing the risk of new competitors.

Wide-moat companies typically derive their advantage from factors such as strong brand recognition, network effects, high customer switching costs, regulatory hurdles and economies of scale. These elements create formidable challenges for new or existing rivals attempting to gain market share. Consequently, these firms often benefit from solid pricing power, stable profit margins, and the capacity to reinvest in their businesses, further reinforcing their long-term competitive edge.

The attraction of investing in wide-moat businesses stems from their ability to deliver steady, long-term returns. In contrast to companies in highly competitive industries, where profits are more vulnerable to pricing pressure and intense rivalry, wide-moat firms tend to show greater stability during economic downturns and market turbulence. Their solid market positions and robust balance sheets enable them to weather challenges that might severely impact less well-protected competitors.

Investing in wide-moat companies provides a solid strategy for building long-term wealth, as these businesses typically produce steady cash flows and deliver shareholder value through dividend payments and stock price growth. While no investment is entirely risk-free, companies with strong economic moats provide a level of durability that many investors seek in an ever-changing market. items.t: Moody’s and FactSet stocks slide on S&P Global’s weak 2026 outlook
sum: Investing.com -- Moody's Corporation (NYSE:MCO) stock fell 5%, FactSet Research (NYSE:FDS) dropped 2%, and MSCI Inc (NYSE:MSCI) declined 2.7% Tuesday as investors reacted to disappointing guidance from industry peer S&P Global.

The financial data and analytics companies all moved lower in sympathy with S&P Global (NYSE:SPGI), which tumbled as much as 13% after reporting quarterly results and forward-looking guidance that missed analyst estimates. The negative sentiment spread across the sector, hitting other major financial information providers.

S&P Global's forecast for fiscal year 2026 earnings per share of $19.40-$19.65 fell short of the $19.96 consensus estimate. The company also projected organic constant currency revenue growth of 6.0% to 8.0% and reported revenue growth of 6.6% to 8.6%.

Market participants appeared concerned that the challenges facing S&P Global could signal broader headwinds for the entire financial data and analytics industry, prompting the selloff in related stocks.

Moody's, which provides credit ratings, research, and risk analysis services, is scheduled to report its own quarterly earnings next Wednesday. Investors will be watching closely to see if Moody's results reflect similar challenges or if the company can differentiate itself from its struggling peer.

The financial information services sector has generally benefited from increased demand for data and analytics in recent years, but today's market reaction suggests growing concerns about future growth prospects and valuation levels across the industry.

NVIDIA ascends to Aa1 status at Moody’s on AI infrastructure dominance
sum: Investing.com -- Moody's Ratings has elevated NVIDIA Corporation's (NASDAQ:NVDA) senior unsecured rating to Aa1, marking a significant milestone in the chipmaker's financial evolution. The credit agency simultaneously maintained a positive outlook, suggesting further upward mobility is possible as the firm solidifies its grip on the artificial intelligence sector.

The upgrade is underpinned by NVIDIA's formidable presence within the rapidly expanding data center ecosystem and its robust liquidity position. Analysts point to the company's industry-leading graphics processing units and proprietary software as the primary engines driving this superior credit profile.

"The Aa1 rating and the positive outlook reflect the rapidly growing size of the data center AI infrastructure market and our expectation that NVIDIA will maintain a dominant position in that market driven by its industry-leading innovations," stated Raj Joshi, Moody's Senior Vice President. This leadership is further bolstered by a developer community of nearly 6 million, which deepens the company's competitive moat through a vast library of domain-specific applications.

Financial projections for the semiconductor giant remain aggressive, with revenues expected to climb from $213 billion in fiscal 2026 to $326 billion the following year. Free cash flow is anticipated to see a corresponding surge, potentially reaching $149 billion as the demand for accelerated computing persists.

Despite the upgrade, the credit agency highlighted risks stemming from a high concentration of revenue among a small group of U.S. hyperscale customers. These large-scale clients are increasingly developing internal silicon programs, which could eventually challenge NVIDIA's premium-priced data center offerings.

"The company is strongly positioned to capitalize on the rising demand for accelerated computing in data centers with its industry-leading graphics processing units (GPUs), central processing units, data processing units, networking, and CUDA software technologies," Joshi added. However, external factors such as domestic electricity supply bottlenecks for data centers could act as a near-term constraint on product demand.
